extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Plato / readers of political philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: A prose commentary/exposition of Plato's Republic (Books IV–V), extracting and discussing prescriptive principles for an ideal State and the corresponding psychology/virtues of the individual. Emphasises education, division of labour, cardinal virtues, gender roles, and communal family arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of education for the State
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the guardians take care of education, and education will take care of all other things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without proper education the State cannot make progress; laws and minute enactments are unnecessary in a well-educated State and useless in a bad one. Education is the 'ground' upon which the 'dye' of laws fixes right opinions (dyed colours analogy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave religion to the proper authority (Delphic/Apollo)
rubrics_metrics.description: To Apollo the god of Delphi we leave the ordering of the greatest of all things—that is to say, religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religion should be based on the highest conception of the gods and maintain the true national (Hellenic) type; no foreign god shall be supreme in the realms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty (first) before individual happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: First duty, then happiness, is the natural order of our moral ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citizens are to be guardians, not holiday-makers; the State's principal aim is the well-being/order of the State, not making individuals happy. Utility is a useful corrective but not the historical basis of morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility as a secondary corrective
rubrics_metrics.description: The utilitarian principle is valuable as a corrective of error ... it is the second principle, often of easier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility may coincide with right, but 'the greatest happiness' is not the true foundation of ethics; the moral law (right) has priority though utility is useful in many ordinary cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four cardinal virtues for State and individual
rubrics_metrics.description: The State will contain all the four virtues—wisdom, courage, temperance, justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each virtue corresponds to a class in the State and a part of the soul; together they constitute political virtue and the health/beauty of the soul.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labour as basis of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice = every one having his own; the great object of government is that every man should do his own business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injustice is every man doing another's business (e.g., a cobbler becoming a guardian). Justice is the order by which all classes do their proper work and cooperate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom concentrated in a small ruling class (guardians)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardians ... are a small class in number ... but in them is concentrated the wisdom of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy/advice for the whole State is a special skill distinct from crafts; selecting wise guardians ensures the whole State is wise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political/civilized courage as fixed right opinion about dangers
rubrics_metrics.description: Courage ... is the never-failing salvation of the opinions which law and education have prescribed concerning dangers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like dye fixed on a properly prepared ground, right opinions (laid by education and law) resist soap of pleasure or lye of pain; call this 'political' or 'civilized' courage to distinguish from mere animal bravery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance as harmony/mastery of better principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperance suggests the idea of harmony ... the better principle in a man masters the worse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperance is diffused through the whole State, making dwellers 'of one mind' and attuning classes (upper/middle/lower) like strings of an instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice as universal order of the whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice is the perfect order by which all natures and classes do their own business ... a universal virtue of the whole soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice is more abstract than other virtues and the foundation to which they are referred; it binds the chords of the soul together producing harmonious action in life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tripartite soul corresponding to State classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The soul is divided into rational, irascible (spirit/passion), and concupiscent elements; each part corresponds to a class in the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason (rulers), spirit/passion (warriors), desire (producers) must be harmonized by education (music and gymnastic). Evidence for distinct faculties is given by contradictory impulses (e.g., thirst vs. reason).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and nature of the irascible/spirit faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Passion or spirit is the ally of reason ... the foundation of courage; it is indignant at wrong and sustains men under unjust suffering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This faculty differs from mere anger; it tends to side with reason and underlies 'righteous indignation' and moral/military courage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue as health of the soul; vice as disease
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is the health and beauty and well-being of the soul, and vice is the disease and weakness and deformity of the soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Just practices produce justice as healthy practices produce health; injustice is insubordination of inferior elements akin to disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the size of the State (small polis model)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement that the State should be limited in size, after the traditional model of a Greek state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The smallness of Hellenic cities is converted into a principle: a whole (manageable polity) underlies good politics and art; overlarge states undermine the desired order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians should be watch-dogs and include women
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardians of our state are to be watch-dogs ... dogs are not divided into hes and shes ... if women are to have the same employments as men, they must have the same education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women should be taught music, gymnastics, and the art of war; good women chosen as guardians alongside men; public ridicule of such equality is to be disregarded as mere wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership and communal living of guardians' families
rubrics_metrics.description: After selection the guardians will dwell in common houses and have their meals in common ... brothers, sisters, parents will be treated as such publicly so that family names become reality in civic ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private family ties are suppressed to produce unity: children and wives in common, common meals, and shared duties to eliminate private interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-managed mating and controlled reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulers will contrive that the brave and the fair come together ... the offspring of the one must be reared, and of the other destroyed; by lots the rulers will make it seem like chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers act as 'physicians of the State' and may need to use 'falsehood' (noble lies) to implement pairing, hymeneal festivals timed for population, and selection to preserve the quality of the 'flock.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal child-rearing with anonymity of parentage
rubrics_metrics.description: When children are born, the offspring of the brave and fair will be carried to an enclosure ... The mothers will be brought to the fold and will suckle the children; care however must be taken that none of them recognise their own offspring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nurses and attendants manage night duties; parents do not know their children; this anonymity supports unity and equal civic identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age limits and regulated timing for procreation
rubrics_metrics.description: The parents ought to be in the prime of life ... for a man ... from twenty-five ... to fifty-five; and at twenty years for a woman—from twenty to forty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in hymeneals outside specified ages is impiety; marriages outside consent of rulers are forbidden for those in prime reproductive ages. Degrees of affinity are defined by timing after espousals (seven or nine months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of the State as highest good; abolish private interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest good of a State is unity; the greatest evil, discord and distraction. There will be unity where there are no private pleasures or pains or interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common property and family among guardians mean that 'if one member suffers all the members suffer', producing civic sensitivity and preventing faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders should be above ambition and prize national character
rubrics_metrics.description: The true leader of men must be above the motives of ambition, and national character is of greater value than material comfort and prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher class statesmen have idealism (Pericles/Anaxagoras example); laws and appeals to truth and right should not be sacrificed to immediate material interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid minute enactments; legislate broad principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Minute enactments are superfluous in good states, and are useless in bad ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation should not try to enter into particulars of every habit; good education and broad laws suffice; micromanagement by law is either unnecessary or ineffective.
